title: Polynomial-Time Encoding After Variable Relabeling
statement: Let $\varphi$ be a CNF formula over natural-number-indexed variables, and let $w(z,j)$ assign a natural number to each bit string $z$ and natural number $j$. Suppose that for every $j<N(\varphi)$, where $N(\varphi)$ is the variable count of $\varphi$, the unary encoding of $w(z,j)$ is polynomial-time computable. Then the function sending $z$ to the fragment encoding of the formula obtained by relabeling each variable index $j$ of $\varphi$ by $w(z,j)$ is polynomial-time computable.
hypotheses_covered: A CNF formula $\varphi$ over natural-number-indexed variables.
A function $w$ from bit strings and natural numbers to natural numbers.
For every $j<N(\varphi)$, the unary encoding of $w(z,j)$ is polynomial-time computable.
